title: Wicks, Bodies & Closes
hook: I don't care about the wick. I need the candle to close through the level.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to tell the difference between price reaching a level and price accepting it.

blocks.heading: Where price traveled and where price actually closed are two different pieces of information

beats.heading: Reached ≠ accepted
beats.body: A wick shows price reached an area. A close shows price accepted (or rejected) it. Those are not the same claim.

beats.heading: This matters far beyond this lesson
beats.body: Later in the Academy, an entire entry model is built around the rule that a candle has to close past a level, not just poke a wick through it.

left.label: Wick
points: Can be misleading on its own

right.label: Close
points: What later entry rules are built on

blocks.heading: Wick vs close, side by side
blocks.prompt: A candle wicks above a key high but closes back below it. See what the wick did NOT hold.

config.caption: Tap "Show the rejection" to see what the wick did not hold

blocks.quote: I don't care about the wick. I need the candle to close through the level. Say that back to yourself every time you're tempted to react to a wick.

questions.question: Price takes a previous high with a wick but closes back below it. Has bullish structure necessarily been confirmed?
options: No — a wick shows price reached the level, but only a close through it shows acceptance
Yes — any candle touching above the high confirms the break
It depends only on the candle's color
questions.why: Reaching a level and accepting past it are two different claims.

questions.question: A wick tells you where price ___. A close tells you where price accepted.
questions.why: The wick is just the extreme reached — not proof of acceptance.

blocks.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "Why doesn't a wick above a level count as a break?" How would you explain it to her?

takeaways: A wick shows reach; a close shows acceptance.
Price can wick past a level and still close back below it — that's not a break.
Close-based confirmation is the rule you'll build entries around later.
remember: I don't care about the wick. I need the close.
